proposed_feature.name: train_delta_transfer_similarity_e267
proposed_feature.description: For each (p,g), compute a weighted average of training deltas for gene g across training perturbations, where weights are the cosine similarity between the target gene of p and the target gene of each training perturbation in gene set space.
proposed_feature.implementation_hint: Build gene set membership vectors for all target genes. For each p, compute cosine similarity with each training target. Use these as weights to average train_delta[:, g]. Exclude p if in training.
proposed_feature.mechanism: Perturbations with similar target gene functions produce similar downstream expression changes.

hypothesis.title: Train delta similarity transfer
hypothesis.hypothesis: Perturbations targeting genes with similar training response profiles to the target produce similar effects on gene g.
hypothesis.rationale: train_delta is unread as a raw input. Current model uses mean_response (average delta) but not the full matrix. A feature that transfers response patterns from similar training perturbations could capture unseen perturbation effects. For each (p,g), compute the similarity between target p and each training perturbation based on their target gene features (e.g., gene set overlap), then weight their training deltas for gene g.

proposed_feature.name: gene_set_similarity_transfer_e177
proposed_feature.description: For each perturbation p, compute a weighted average of training delta responses from other perturbations, where weights are the Jaccard similarity between the gene sets of p's target and the other target's gene sets.
proposed_feature.implementation_hint: For each target gene, compute its gene set membership vector. Compute Jaccard similarity with all training perturbation targets. For each (p,g), compute predicted delta as sum over training perturbations q of similarity(p,q) * train_delta[q,g] / sum(similarity). Use leave-one-out to avoid using p's own response.
proposed_feature.mechanism: Perturbations of genes with similar functions (shared gene sets) may produce similar expression changes.

hypothesis.title: Risky: transfer from similar perturbations using gene set similarity
hypothesis.hypothesis: Using a similarity-weighted average of training responses from perturbations whose target genes share many gene sets with the current perturbation target will improve predictions for unseen perturbations.
hypothesis.rationale: This is a transfer learning idea that uses gene_sets in a novel way. It is risky because it may overfit or be too complex, but could capture perturbation similarity.
